title: When is idli-vada said for the tenth time?
description: The idli-vada numbers are the multiples of fifteen, so the tenth one is fifteen times ten. A check shows that the number is a multiple of three and of five.
teaching_notes: One idea: the nth idli-vada number is the nth multiple of fifteen. Watch for students who add the count to fifteen instead of multiplying.

source: Figure it Out box 1, Q1, p.108
video_script.why: The child sees that the idli-vada numbers are the multiples of fifteen, so the tenth time is the tenth multiple of fifteen.
video_script.substitution: Take the nth idli-vada as the nth multiple of fifteen.
video_script.anchor: children playing the idli-vada game, with the idli-vada numbers written in a row
video_script.payoff_line: Idli-vada is said for the tenth time at one hundred and fifty

final_answer.spoken: idli-vada is said for the tenth time at one hundred and fifty

maths_rules: idli is said at multiples of 3, vada at multiples of 5, idli-vada at multiples of both, the multiples of 15
1st idli-vada 15, 2nd 30, 3rd 45; each is 15 more than the one before
10th idli-vada is the 10th multiple of 15: 15 x 10 = 150
check: 150 = 3 x 50 and 150 = 5 x 30, so 150 is a multiple of 3 and of 5
video_script.design: One idea: the tenth idli-vada is the tenth multiple of fifteen. Same method as the book example: the common multiples are the multiples of one number.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a circle of children and a question mark

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.game: the words idli, vada and idli-vada appear in turn
marks.ask: the question appears with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the idli-vada game.
<bookmark mark='game'/>Children say idli for multiples of three, vada for multiples of five, and idli-vada for both.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>At what number is idli-vada said for the tenth time?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the idli-vada numbers 15, 30, 45 are written in a row, each jump of 15 marked

marks.way: the example from the book is pointed to
marks.list: the numbers 15, 30 and 45 are written in a row
marks.gap: a jump of 15 is marked between each pair

narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>We use the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Idli-vada is said at fifteen, thirty, forty five, and on.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>Each one is fifteen more than the one before.

beats.on_screen: Given: idli-vada is said at the common multiples of 3 and 5: 15, 30, 45, ...

marks.given: the rule and the first numbers are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, idli-vada is said at the common multiples of three and five.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number where idli-vada is said for the 10th time

marks.find: the words To find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number for the tenth idli-vada.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 15 = 15 x 1, 30 = 15 x 2, 45 = 15 x 3; the idli-vada numbers are the multiples of 15

marks.see: each number is written as 15 times a counting number
marks.times: the times 1, 2 and 3 glow in gold

narration: <bookmark mark='see'/>Step one, see what these numbers are. Fifteen, thirty and forty five are multiples of fifteen.
<bookmark mark='times'/>The first is fifteen times one. The second is fifteen times two. The third is fifteen times three.

marks.tenth: 15 x 10 is written under the list

narration: <bookmark mark='tenth'/>Step two, the tenth idli-vada is fifteen times ten.
<bookmark mark='val'/>Fifteen times ten is one hundred and fifty.

beats.on_screen: Check: 150 = 3 x 50 and 150 = 5 x 30, so 150 is a multiple of 3 and of 5

marks.both: 150 = 5 x 30 is written and both lines get a tick

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step three, put the number back. One hundred and fifty is three times fifty.
<bookmark mark='both'/>It is also five times thirty, so it is a multiple of three and of five.

beats.on_screen: Answer: idli-vada is said for the tenth time at 150
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Idli-vada is said for the tenth time at one hundred and fifty.
